precepts.text: The book of the law shall not depart from thy mouth; meditate day and night to observe and do it, and thy way shall be prosperous.
precepts.point: Where should we make our refuge? It begins with meditating on the scriptures, which is why the four chapters a day has been set up.
precepts.why:
“in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.” Where should we make our refuge? It begins with meditating on the scriptures. “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.”

The book of the law does not depart from thy mouth; you meditate in it day and night to observe and do it, and thy way is made prosperous. That is why the four chapters a day has been set up. The refuge under his wings starts there.

precepts.text: He that dwells in the secret place of the Most High abides under the shadow of the Almighty, and His truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
precepts.point: Where should we make our refuge? It begins with meditating on the scriptures, which is why the four chapters a day has been set up.
precepts.why:
“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” That is the shadow of the wings David makes his refuge in. “I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust. Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.”

“He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.” Under his wings, covered with his feathers, and his truth is the shield and buckler. That is where the refuge is until these calamities be overpast, and it begins with meditating on the scriptures, the truth that shields.

precepts.text: They that feared the Most High spake often one to another, a safety net of communication so our conversations stay in the law.
precepts.point: Where should we make our refuge? It begins with meditating on the scriptures, which is why the four chapters a day has been set up.
precepts.why:
“Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.” They that feared the Most High spoke often one to another, and he heard it and wrote a book of remembrance for them.

That speaking often one to another is a safety net of communication, so our conversations stay in the law. Meditating on the scriptures day and night and talking them over with the brethren is how we make our refuge in the shadow of his wings until the calamities be overpast.

precepts.text: The Most High caused a great apparition and sent a rider and two mighty young men who scourged Heliodorus continually when he came to rob the treasury.
precepts.point: When it says He shall send from heaven and save me, look at the history of Heliodorus, who came to take all the funds out of the temple true to the nature of Edom the grape gatherer, and the Most High sent two angels to give the heathen a righteous beating.
precepts.why:
“He shall send from heaven, and save me from the reproach of him that would swallow me up.” Look at the history of Heliodorus, who came to take all the funds out of the temple, true to the nature of Edom the grape gatherer. “Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, the Lord of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of God, and fainted, and were sore afraid.”

“For there appeared unto them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and smote at Heliodorus with his forefeet”. Then “two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.” The Most High sent two angels to give the heathen a righteous beating. That is what it looks like when he sends from heaven and saves from the one who would swallow you up.

precepts.text: Seeing thou hast been scourged from heaven, declare unto all men the mighty power of God.
precepts.point: When it says He shall send from heaven and save me, look at the history of Heliodorus, who came to take all the funds out of the temple true to the nature of Edom the grape gatherer, and the Most High sent two angels to give the heathen a righteous beating.
precepts.why: When Heliodorus was scourged, the young men told him: “seeing that thou hast been scourged from heaven, declare unto all men the mighty power of God. And when they had spoken these words, they appeared no more.” Scourged from heaven: that is the Most High sending from heaven to save his people from the reproach of the heathen who came to rob the treasury. Heliodorus had to declare the mighty power of God to all men, and God sent forth his mercy and his truth to his people.

precepts.text: The Son of man comes in the clouds with power, and sends His angels to gather His elect, us, from the four winds because we have been scattered.
precepts.point: When it says He shall send from heaven and save me, look at the history of Heliodorus, who came to take all the funds out of the temple true to the nature of Edom the grape gatherer, and the Most High sent two angels to give the heathen a righteous beating.
precepts.why:
He shall send from heaven and save me. At the end it is the Son of man himself: “then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” He comes in the clouds with power.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” He sends his angels to gather his elect, us, from the four winds, because we have been scattered. As he sent angels from heaven against Heliodorus, he sends them from heaven to gather his people and save them from him that would swallow them up. God shall send forth his mercy and his truth.

precepts.text: The blessed man delights in the law and meditates day and night, and is like a tree planted by the rivers of water whose leaf shall not wither.
precepts.point: We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.
precepts.why:
“My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise.” A fixed heart is the tree planted by the rivers of water that will not be swayed. “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.”

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.” Doctrines will not pull that man out; he will not be hasty to credit somebody by their looks or their money, and no one takes his crown. David in the spirit says his heart is fixed even though all these enemies come against him, and he awakes early to praise. We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and the beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.

precepts.text: It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, His compassions fail not and are new every morning.
precepts.point: We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.
precepts.why:
“For thy mercy is great unto the heavens, and thy truth unto the clouds.” “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed; his compassions fail not and are new every morning.

That is why David says “I myself will awake early” to praise him. His mercy is great unto the heavens and new every morning, so the fixed heart sings and gives praise among the people and among the nations.

points: He asks for mercy, for his soul trusts in the Most High, and makes his refuge in the shadow of His wings until the calamities be overpast.
Where should we make our refuge? It begins with meditating on the scriptures, which is why the four chapters a day has been set up.
He cries unto the Most High that performs all things for him, who shall send from heaven and save him from the reproach of him that would swallow him up, sending forth His mercy and truth.

When it says He shall send from heaven and save me, look at the history of Heliodorus, who came to take all the funds out of the temple true to the nature of Edom the grape gatherer, and the Most High sent two angels to give the heathen a righteous beating.
His soul is among lions and among the sons of men whose teeth are spears and arrows and their tongue a sharp sword, yet he cries that the Most High be exalted above the heavens.
They prepared a net for his steps and digged a pit before him, but they are fallen into the midst of it themselves.
David in the spirit says his heart is fixed even though all these enemies come against him; he will sing and give praise and awake early.

A fixed heart is the tree planted by the rivers of water that will not be swayed. Doctrines will not pull you out; you will not be hasty to credit somebody by their looks or their money, and no one takes your crown.

We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.
